subsections.title: PROJECT OBJECTIVES
subsections.content:
To provide simple, engaging, and practical education that builds skills, confidence, and positive mindset among children, youth, and women. Key Objectives:

- Make learning fun and interactive instead of traditional methods.

- Build life skills such as communication, teamwork, and problem -solving.

- Help youth gain practical skills that can lead to income opportunities.

- Increase self -confidence and encourage self -expression.

- Reach communities in simple and flexible ways, even without strong infrastructure.

subsections.title: IMPACT ON EVANGELISM
subsections.content:
The project builds trust first, allowing evangelism to happen naturally through relationships and daily interaction. Key Impact:

- Connect with youth in a way they understand and enjoy.

- Create safe and welcoming environments for open conversations.

- Share values through actions, not only words.

- Build long -term relationships within the community .

subsections.title: Problem Statement and Medical Challenge
subsections.content: With Medical facilities being limited, STP offers limited Medical Care and the services provided are very basic which has led to outbreak of some diseases. Among the Most Commonly Spread Diseases in STP are: 1- Tuberculosis (TB): Which is a bacterial disease easily communicable in the first few weeks of visible symptoms. 2- Malaria: spreads through mosquitoes, is an endemic for most impoverished African countries, including Sao Tome Principe. 3- Cholera: is actively transmitted in many impoverished countries, including Sao Tome and Principe. Other common medical Conditions include Obesity, HIV & Necrotizing cellulitis

subsections.title: Impact
subsections.content:
- Cholera: Though Not an endemic, there are sporadic outbreaks from time to

time especially in districts with poor clear water supply

- Malaria: there are hundreds of cases every year but low mortality rate

- Uncomplicated malaria: usually can be treated locally if you reach a

clinic or hospital.

- Severe malaria or complications: more difficult, requires advanced

care and referral capacity are limited

- Tuberculosis (TB):

- Exists there at a notable rate, and treatment is accessible, but

adherence and continuity of care remain a problem. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), in 2016, there was a 63% decrease in TB mortality since 2000, a 95% detection rate for the  disease and a 78% success rate in treating patients.

subsections.title: Mission Objectives: Healthcare and Capacity Building
subsections.content:
The mission's goals are divided into immediate relief and long -term structural improvement to address the country's limited medical facilities and basic care services. Short -Term Objectives (Immediate Relief)

- Disease Prevention and Outbreak Reduction:  Provide essential vaccinations

and proper medical treatments to all age groups (infants to seniors) to mitigate the spread of endemic diseases like Malaria, Cholera, and Tuberculosis.

- Public Health Awareness:  Launch multi -platform campaigns (posters, videos,

and tutorials) in schools and public spaces to educate the public on safety protocols and encourage behavioral changes that improve health outcomes.

- Specialized Youth Workshops:  Implement interactive programs like "Super

Teeth Heroes" (dental care) and "Clean Water Warriors" (cholera prevention) to engage children ages 5 –12 in proactive hygiene habits. Long -Term Objectives (Sustainability)

- Local Empowerment through ToTs:  Conduct "Training of Trainers" (ToT )

programs for residents aged 20 –40 in basic nursing and first aid to ensure faster emergency response times and local autonomy in healthcare.

- Pharmaceutical Supply Chain Integration:  Establish formal legal agreements

between Egyptian pharmaceutical providers and local STP authorities (Ministry of Health and CAME) to ensure the consistent procurement of essential medicines.

- Economic Opportunity:  Create job opportunities for local residents by

equipping them with recognized medical competencies and skills.

subsections.title: Impact on Coptic Orthodox Church Evangelism
subsections.content: The medical mission serves as a practical expression of the Church’s ministry, potentially transforming its evangelistic reach in São Tomé and Príncipe through several key channels: 1. Building Social Trust through Service By addressing the "Problem Statement" of limited medical care, the Church demonstrates a tangible commitment to the well -being of the Santomean people. This "mercy ministry" can open doors for spiritual dialogue in communities that might otherwise be hesit ant to engage with a new ecclesiastical presence. 2. Holistic Community Engagement The mission targets every demographic —from children in schools to seniors in hospitals. This broad reach allows the Church to establish a presence across various social strata, moving beyond simple preaching to becoming a vital community partner in public health. 3. Sustainable Presence and Integration The focus on long -term solutions, such as ToT programs and pharmaceutical agreements, ensures that the Church’s impact is not seen as a "one -off" event. By investing in the local workforce and legal healthcare framework, the Church fosters deep -rooted relationships with both the government and the citizenry, providing a stable platform for long -term evangelism. 4. Direct Outreach via Educational Content Interactive workshops and "Sketch Ideas" provide a unique opportunity to blend health education with Christian values of stewardship and care for the body. Programs like "Protect Your Mind & Eyes" for teens allow the Church to provide guidance on modern li festyle challenges, positioning it as a relevant voice for the younger generation.
